title: Testing My Modded C8 ZR1 + Cheap Car Challenge Rules Meeting
coverage: full transcript read (0:00-45:55); 0:00-16:49 track test (giveaway ZR1 + C8 ZR1), 16:49-45:55 CRC3 rules meeting

context.date_stated: giveaway ends 'tonight' April 27 (2026 implied by later CRC3 videos)

event.name: Sick Summer-style drag-and-drive (caption 'six summer'); held in Michigan

previous_cars_referenced.fact: Previous challenge cars: the 240, 'Lumberjack' and the Mustang; this round: new cars, new engines

rules.fact: Budget $15,000 per team (alternatives $12.5k / $30k floated and rejected); budget earlier framed as $5k car + $10k build
Free safety items: roll cage (all cars get 8.50-spec cages), driver race seat, driver seat belts; seat cushions debated; everything else costs money
Term 'safety equipment' narrowed to seat belts etc. after Jackstand counted head studs as safety equipment last time
Race director Ryan (caption 'Ryan warning') is sole judge of fair market value; if you paid less (e.g. $200 for a $500 converter) the higher FMV is charged; no arguing

Vehicle: any car at fair market value (even a non-running roller is valued by Ryan); must arrive unmodified - no upgrades, teams must do every upgrade themselves; stock-car / $5k-$7.5k car caps were debated but not adopted
Parts priced at brand-new price when new; no sponsorships of any kind (incl. wheels/tires)
No selling, bartering or trading of your own parts
No free spare engines; any replacement part (engine, lug nuts, wheel studs, tires) comes out of budget; you may bring a spare engine but pay for it if used
Tires come out of budget (new set ~ $900 cited)
Costs tracked on an Excel spreadsheet
Machine shop work charged at the real shop labor rate
Own labor is free; outside help that touches the car is charged at that person's/shop labor rate (50% and 75% floated, example $110/h trans shop, $100/h Cameron)
Tuning: if anyone else touches your laptop or carburetor it counts as outsourced tuning, flat $500 for the week (based on Nate's quote)
Over-budget penalty: +0.5 s added to that day's average per $100 over
If the car breaks you must keep going and fix it within budget; if you are out of money, the only thing you may buy/borrow is a moped
Each team gets a fuel cell (similar size within ~1 gal, no pump included) so stock tanks are not used; details to be settled when cars are bought
Scoring: full 5-day average ET decides; final-day shootout is bragging rights only
Proposed loser penalty: losers drive their cars from Michigan back to Florida
Previous challenge noted: last time it was argued whether single best pass or average decided it

dyno.note: Overboost protection: on dyno would make ~1,003 and a limiter held it there

wheels_tires.drag: Boost District beadlock wheels sized for ZR1 brakes, 11 in wide, Nitto drag radial 315/35R20 rear (stock rear wheels said to be 21 in); front ~295

passes.note: pulls hard then lays over - suspected overboost protection under load
launch turned up; hot day, car parked two months

failures.part: Catalytic converter over-temperature code -> timing pulled
failures.cause: tables not available when first tuned

targets.et: 8s on a street car (others already running 8s)

notes.fact: Previously spun tires every drag strip visit on stock rubber despite strong street performance

base_vehicle.generation: not stated here; supercharged ('big blower'); ZTuZc5Sp1fo refers to 'our C7 ZR1 winner'

notes.fact: Spray wax claimed worth two tenths (joke, 'Talladega tested')
